A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the quark model is a useful tool to understand the hadron spectra, the hadron–nucleon interaction, and the hadron–meson interaction in the low-energy region.

the constituent quark model, when properly implemented, can provide a good description of hadron spectroscopic data and the hadron–meson and hadron–nucleon interactions in a unified framework, without the need to introduce ad hoc models for the interaction.

the quark model, as a first step, is a good starting point to understand the low-energy hadronic phenomenology, but the model has to be extended to include the effect of the higher order Fock state components.

a coherent picture can be obtained from a single model, which can be used to understand a wide variety of low-energy hadron phenomena, including the hadron spectrum and the hadron–nucleus scattering cross section.
